profile: Turns crude oil and renewable raw materials, such as waste and plant oils, into fuels and other products. It sells renewable diesel and sustainable aviation fuel mainly to businesses and wholesale buyers, while also selling conventional fuels and operating fuel stations in Finland and the Baltic countries.

otherClaims.label: Debt and other claims, less cash

summary: Neste Oyj (NESTE.HE, NASDAQ Helsinki) turns crude oil and renewable raw materials into fuels, sustainable aviation fuel and other products, and runs nearly 1,000 fuel stations in Finland and the Baltic countries. The share price was 28.4 EUR on 3 November 2026, against market capitalisation of EUR 21.8bn and enterprise value of EUR 25.7bn. In this Valuatum market report dated 3 November 2026, the company is assessed through the businesses represented in today's price rather than through a target price or recommendation. Analysts' 2028 forecast is EUR 23.5bn of net sales and EUR 2.6bn of operating profit.

Oil products represent 17.6 EUR per share, or 52% of the EUR 33.5 per share attributed to the businesses before debt, at 13.2x 2028 operating profit. Renewable fuels contribute 12.3 EUR per share, or 37%, at 8.8x 2028 operating profit, while fuel retail and services contribute 3.65 EUR per share, or 11%, at 5.5x. Debt and other claims, less cash, reduce the total by 5.09 EUR per share to 28.4 EUR. Together, the businesses cost about 10x 2028 operating profit, broadly matching listed peers.

The overall price sits alongside peers at about 10x 2028 operating profit, while each business is only 2% of the way from its peer median towards the cheapest peer. The important question is whether forecast margins can replace 2025's weaker outcomes: oil products move from 4.7% to 12%, renewable fuels from 1.93% to 11%, and fuel retail from 1.9% to 10%. Rotterdam's start-up by end-2027, Porvoo utilisation after its turnaround, refining margins and recurring retail profit are the key evidence.

thesis.title: What you pay for
thesis.text: Oil products and renewable fuels make up 89% of the EUR 33.5 per share assigned to the businesses before debt: 17.6 EUR and 12.3 EUR respectively. Their 13.2x and 8.8x 2028 operating-profit multiples leave the share price dependent on forecast margins.

thesis.title: Peer comparison
thesis.text: The businesses together cost about 10x 2028 operating profit, matching listed peers overall. Oil products sits at 13.2x against a 13.4x industry median, while renewable fuels and fuel retail are both at their 8.8x and 5.5x medians.

thesis.title: What to watch
thesis.text: Rotterdam's expected start-up by end-2027 and its revised EUR 3.0bn project cost are central to renewable-fuels capacity. The next evidence is whether 2026 sales and margins follow forecast, after an eight-week Rotterdam shutdown and Porvoo's turnaround.

valuePools.name: Oil products
valuePools.economics: 13.2x 2028 operating profit · EUR 1,021m 2028 operating profit · peers about 13.4x
valuePools.text: Oil products refines crude oil at Porvoo and sells diesel, petrol, jet fuel, marine fuel and other products to retailers, distributors, oil majors, traders and industrial customers. Outside-customer sales were EUR 6.9bn in 2025, with 11.9 million tonnes sold, including 5.7 million tonnes of middle distillates. The business produced EUR 325m of operating profit at a 4.7% margin in 2025. The price assigns 17.6 EUR per share, or 52% of the EUR 33.5 per share attributed to the businesses before debt, at 13.2x its EUR 1,021m 2028 operating-profit allocation. That allocation requires a 12% margin on EUR 8.6bn of sales. The 2025 refining margin was USD 14.0 per barrel, against USD 6.5 per barrel of Porvoo production cost, while the third quarter of 2026 reached USD 48.2 per barrel with 51% utilisation during the turnaround.

valuePools.name: Renewable fuels
valuePools.economics: 8.8x 2028 operating profit · EUR 1,070m 2028 operating profit · peers about 8.8x
valuePools.text: Renewable fuels sells renewable diesel, sustainable aviation fuel and related products mainly to businesses and wholesale buyers. Outside-customer sales were EUR 7.8bn in 2025, including 3.2 million tonnes of renewable diesel and 0.9 million tonnes of aviation fuel. The business reported EUR 151m of operating profit, a 1.93% margin, while its comparable sales margin was USD 411 per tonne and plant utilisation was 73%. The price assigns 12.3 EUR per share, or 37% of the EUR 33.5 per share attributed to the businesses before debt, at 8.8x the EUR 1,070m 2028 operating-profit allocation. That requires an 11% margin on EUR 9.7bn of sales. Third-quarter 2026 performance was stronger, with a USD 1,068 per tonne margin, 97% utilisation and record sales of 1.29 million tonnes, but the Rotterdam expansion now costs about EUR 3.0bn.

valuePools.name: Fuel retail and services
valuePools.economics: 5.5x 2028 operating profit · EUR 511m 2028 operating profit · peers about 5.5x
valuePools.text: Fuel retail and services sells fuels, electric-vehicle charging and related services through nearly 1,000 stations in Finland and the Baltic countries, as well as to transport and industrial customers. Outside-customer sales were EUR 4.3bn in 2025, including EUR 3,336m from Finland and EUR 974m from the Baltic countries. Operating profit was EUR 82m at a 1.9% margin. The price assigns 3.65 EUR per share, or 11% of the EUR 33.5 per share attributed to the businesses before debt, at 5.5x the EUR 511m 2028 operating-profit allocation. That allocation requires a 10% margin on EUR 5.3bn of sales, well above the 2025 result and reported peer margins of 6.1% at Alimentation Couche-Tard, 3.7% at Murphy USA and 1.3% at ARKO. January-to-September 2026 profit was EUR 96m, supported partly by inventory gains.

coreAnalysis.heading: What the price pays for
coreAnalysis.text: The share price is built mainly on two refining and renewable-fuels outcomes. Oil products account for 17.6 EUR per share and renewable fuels for 12.3 EUR, together 89% of the EUR 33.5 per share assigned to the businesses before debt. Fuel retail and services contributes 3.65 EUR, while debt and other claims, less cash, subtract 5.09 EUR to leave 28.4 EUR. The operating-profit assumptions behind those allocations are substantial. Oil products requires EUR 1,021m of 2028 operating profit and a 12% margin on EUR 8.6bn of sales, versus EUR 325m and 4.7% in 2025. Renewable fuels requires EUR 1,070m and an 11% margin on EUR 9.7bn, versus EUR 151m and 1.93%. Fuel retail requires EUR 511m and a 10% margin on EUR 5.3bn, versus EUR 82m and 1.9%. Recent quarterly evidence is stronger in refining and renewable fuels, but the retail result includes inventory gains. The share price is therefore made mostly of normalised or expanded margins rather than simply current reported earnings.

coreAnalysis.heading: Why the price is alongside peers
coreAnalysis.text: The three businesses together cost about 10x analysts' 2028 operating profit, broadly the same as listed peers. Oil products is assigned 13.2x against a 13.4x industry median, within a 5.7x to 18.2x range. Renewable fuels is at 8.8x, equal to the 8.8x median of its 7.0x to 11.5x industry range, and fuel retail is at 5.5x, equal to the 5.5x median between 3.3x and 7.7x. The small overall gap from peer medians reflects uncertainty about the profits being capitalised. Oil products would need to move from a 4.7% 2025 margin to 12%, while renewable fuels would need to reach 11% from 1.93%. Fuel retail would need 10% from 1.9%, above reported margins of 6.1% at Alimentation Couche-Tard, 3.7% at Murphy USA and 1.3% at ARKO. Peer comparisons are also limited: fewer than three listed peers were available for each business, so industry quartiles stand in for the range. VERBIO's 206.0x 2026 P/E is excluded as an outlier from peer medians and averages.

coreAnalysis.heading: What to watch
coreAnalysis.text: The evidence that can change the composition of the share price arrives through operating milestones rather than a change in the stated method. Rotterdam is expected to start by end-2027, adding 1.3 million tonnes of annual capacity and taking the site to 2.7 million tonnes, including 1.2 million tonnes of aviation fuel. The project cost has risen from EUR 2.5bn to about EUR 3.0bn, so a delay would leave less capacity supporting the EUR 1,070m renewable-fuels allocation while the larger investment would count for more. Oil products needs Porvoo to return towards its 90% 2025 utilisation after the turnaround and needs refining margins to remain closer to the third-quarter USD 48.2 per barrel than the 2025 USD 14.0. Fuel retail needs quarterly profit to persist without inventory gains and its margin to approach 10%. The eight-week Rotterdam shutdown in the fourth quarter of 2026 and the 11-week Singapore-line shutdown are immediate production tests. Full-year 2027 results should show whether the forecast margins are becoming operating results.

risks: Renewable-fuels margin reversal (renewable fuels): a return from the third-quarter USD 1,068 per tonne margin towards USD 411 in 2025 would make the EUR 1,070m 2028 operating-profit allocation difficult to reach, with margin per tonne as the early warning.

Rotterdam delay or overrun (renewable fuels): a start-up after end-2027 or further cost above EUR 3.0bn would reduce the capacity reaching the 2028 sales forecast, with project progress and cost updates as the early warning.

Refining-margin normalisation (oil products): a move from USD 48.2 per barrel in the third quarter of 2026 towards USD 14.0 in 2025 would challenge the assumed 12% margin, with margin per barrel as the early warning.
Porvoo under-utilisation (oil products): utilisation below the 90% 2025 level after the turnaround would leave fixed costs spread over less output, with refinery utilisation as the early warning.

Non-recurring retail profit (fuel retail and services): reversal of inventory gains could leave the segment near its 1.9% 2025 margin rather than the 10% 2028 allocation, with quarterly operating profit and inventory-gain commentary as the early warning.
catalysts: Porvoo normal running (near-term, oil products): utilisation close to 90% through 2027 would spread fixed costs across more output and support the assumed margin.
Rotterdam start-up (medium-term, renewable fuels): commissioning by end-2027 would add 1.3 million tonnes of annual capacity and provide a full operating year before 2028.
Sustained renewable margin (near-term, renewable fuels): a margin near USD 1,068 per tonne rather than USD 411 would make the EUR 1,070m 2028 operating-profit allocation more credible.

Recurring retail profitability (near-term, fuel retail and services): operating profit without inventory gains and a margin moving towards 10% would turn the forecast allocation into a reported result.

Performance-improvement delivery (medium-term, oil products and renewable fuels): annual EBITDA improvement continuing above EUR 697m against the 2024 baseline would narrow the gap between reported and forecast margins.

faqs.q: What is Neste's share price made of?
faqs.a: At 28.4 EUR per share, oil products account for 17.6 EUR, renewable fuels for 12.3 EUR and fuel retail and services for 3.65 EUR. Debt and other claims, less cash, subtract 5.09 EUR per share, leaving 28.4 EUR.

faqs.q: Why does Neste trade alongside its peers?
faqs.a: The businesses together cost about 10x analysts' 2028 operating profit, broadly matching peers. Oil products is at 13.2x against a 13.4x industry median, while renewable fuels and fuel retail are at their 8.8x and 5.5x medians.

faqs.q: What do analysts forecast for Neste's sales and profit?
faqs.a: Analysts forecast 2028 net sales of EUR 23,510m, EBITDA of EUR 3,718m, operating profit of EUR 2,602m and net earnings of EUR 2,013m. The forecast EPS is 2.6 EUR and DPS is 2.1 EUR.

The main tests are Rotterdam's expected start-up by end-2027, the project's EUR 3.0bn cost, Porvoo utilisation after its turnaround, refining margins, renewable-fuels margin per tonne and whether fuel-retail profit persists without inventory gains.

faqs.q: How does Valuatum's market report work?
faqs.a: The method keeps analysts' forecasts through 2028, splits group profit between businesses using reported segment results, compares each business with peers using EV/EBIT, and reads today's 28.4 EUR share price back into those businesses after debt and other claims, less cash.
